newsitem.title: USA: Activists block bulldozers in Calif. logging protest.
newsitem.headline: Activists block bulldozers in Calif. logging protest.

text.p: Environmental activists said on Tuesday they locked themselves to bulldozers to block the controversial logging of fallen trees in an ancient redwood forest in northern California.
Six activists locked themselves to bulldozers blocking the Pacific Lumber Co access road to the All Species grove, an old-growth redwood grove, the group Earth First said.
Sheriff's deputies arrested as many as eight activists for their involvement in the protest, Sgt. Pete Ciarabellini said.

He estimated that as many as 1,200 arrests have been made since demonstrations started in mid-September. Over 120 Earth First activists have been arrested in protests over Pacific Lumber Co salvaging, the group said.

California, the U.S. government, MAXXAM Inc, and its subsidiary, Pacific Lumber, reached a tentative agreement last month to set aside two ancient redwood groves for parks, in return for $380 million in cash and land. A moratorium on salvage logging is in place in those two groves.
But in four other old-growth groves, Pacific Lumber is permitted to salvage fallen trees, said Robert Irelan, spokesman for MAXXAM Inc.
"We are just going about our business," he said on Tuesday. "We are removing fallen timber. That is what we are permitted to do and it is precisely what we are doing."
Earth First maintains that fallen trees are an integral part of the forest ecosystem. By removing them, the group said, serious environmental damage was being done.

At 5:25 a.m. local time on Tuesday (8:25 a.m. EDT), 30 activists stopped three bulldozers and a security vehicle by placing themselves in the road to the All Species grove, Earth First said. Using steel boxes and handcuffs, six of the activists locked themselves to the bulldozers, the group said.

Environmentalists have for years fought to preserve the Headwaters grove, the nation's largest privately-owned ancient redwood forest, and five other old-growth redwood groves near Eureka, 300 miles (500 kms) north of San Francisco.
